item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
My recent coming across of a video game where you play as a cat in a city heavily inspired by the Kowloon Walled City has made me curious again of both this SCP and the city in general. I actually looked around on YouTube and Google Images about the city (using its Chinese name "九龍城寨" (jiu long chen zai)), and I found a lot of images and a segment from a Taiwanese talk show about the city on YouTube. Unfortunately the video is in Mandarin (which means 99% of the audience here won't understand it), but even if you don't there's some video footage about the city in that video that really adds to the visual fuel for this story; I highly recommend watching that video if you want a better appreciation of the story here.

To be honest, I thought the references to the triads in this story was a bit of creative licence, until I watched that video which mentioned not only how crime-infested it was, but how there could be actual gun fights between triad members in the lower levels of the city. Not only that, but there was a lot of dodgy and outright-illegal activities in there - unlicensed dentists, gambling dens, heroin dens, opium dens, brothels, unregulated food factories, and the like. Once you know all these the references to the criminal activities here seem tame by comparison.

I also highly recommend looking up on how the interior of Chinese temples look like; being an adherent of Chinese folk religion and Buddhism here I have visited many Chinese temples before, and it really helps with visualising (and better appreciating) the last part of the story when the protagonist goes into the temple in an effort to look for the SCP. It really helps with the creep factor, visualising Chinese temple-style halls and corridors made of "wrong" materials, altars full of statues of deities made of one solid mass of wood, etc.

All in all, a great story. Upvoted.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Only Gears can possibly make even scips with one of the least dangerous abilities mind-numbingly, bone-chillingly, terrifying. Completely innocuous at first glance. I read 184 well before I read this shortly before, since evidently this is linked in the article, and liked it, but thought it was nothing remarkable. Well, overly remarkable. I thought it was a neat little thing that was one of the few harmless things the Foundation contained. Then I read this a little while after. I have since been more than a little terrified of 184. And now I have the ability to upvote them both.

Normal version: Enters room, makes it bigger, changes composition.

Gears version: Enters room, makes it bigger, makes it impossible to leave, and drives you nuts because you're cut off completely from people. Also makes it utterly terrifying.

item.title: Re: Sudden fridge horror.
item.content:encoded: I disagree- or more accurately, I don't think it matters. No matter where he was in the temple when it was destroyed, he was still inside it. Interpret the missing corpse how you will, but I'd wager that anything you introduced to an affected structure could be found in the rubble once you knocked the building down.
